mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the direct foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or registrar of companies in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a qualified notary public in the country of origin. If the country of origin is a Hague Apostille Convention member state: legalize exclusively by a single apostille certificate issued by the designated Competent Authority. If the country of origin is not an Apostille Convention member state: legalize exclusively through the consular legalization route, comprising authentication by the country of origin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed by legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. The Hague Apostille and consular legalization routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the direct foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registrar of companies in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a qualified notary public in the country of origin, then either a single apostille issued by the designated Competent Authority if the country of origin is a Hague Apostille Convention member state, or authentication by the country of origin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs plus consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate if the country of origin is not a member state. The two legalization routes are parallel and must not be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney of the direct foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or authorised corporate representative of the direct foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a qualified notary public in the country of origin. For Hague Apostille Convention member states, attach a single apostille from the designated Competent Authority. For non-member states, attach authentication by the country of origin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and subsequent consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and constitutional documents of the direct foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: As registered with the home jurisdiction company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a qualified notary public in the country of origin; then either a single apostille by the designated Competent Authority if the country of origin is an Apostille Convention member state, or authentication by the country of origin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed by consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate if the country of origin is not a member state. These routes are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the direct foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in the shareholder's home country, signed by an authorised bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the bank officer's signature by a notary public; thereafter, if the country of origin is a Hague Apostille Convention member state, legalize exclusively with a single apostille from the designated Competent Authority; if the country of origin is not a member state, legalize exclusively by authentication with the country of origin's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are separate parallel paths and must never be applied sequentially to the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before formation, every direct and indirect owner, director, legal representative, supervisor, senior manager, signatory and any person holding 25% or more interest must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and SSI/NS-Military End User lists, EU/UK global human rights and financial sanctions lists, China's MOFCOM sanctions lists, domestic terrorist watchlists, and local court judgement enforcement blacklists. Adverse media, PEP status, source of funds, source of wealth, country risk, industry risk, and business relationship risk must be assessed. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs and for investors from high-risk third countries. Continuous transaction monitoring, annual re-screening, risk scoring, and an independent audit trail must be maintained by the compliance officer. For this medium-risk enhanced voice streaming application, additional KYC evidence of app platform licences, IP rights, and app content moderation controls should be obtained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Platform and China National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be expressed in simplified Chinese script. The four-tier naming structure consists of (1) administrative division, (2) a distinctive trade name, (3) the industry or business characteristics describing the ISIC 6311 voice streaming and audio companion social services, and (4) the legal form marker expressed as limited liability company. The foreign investor's name may be transliterated phonetically into simplified Chinese, but it must clearly identify the ultimate owner, avoid misleading similarity to existing registered names, and comply with the SAMR Administrative Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration. An English name may be used in commerce but is not separately registered and cannot create a separate legal identity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days of an online rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration application with the market regulatory authority at the next higher level under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, attaching the SAMR decision, a proposed revised name, and a supporting explanation. If administrative reconsideration is not pursued, administrative litigation may be filed within six months in the competent people's court. The applicant should correct any transliteration conflict, obtain a written consent letter from the prior name holder if similarity arises from a trade name or trademark, and resubmit through the same portal with a different third-tier industry description.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE in the ISIC 6311 voice streaming and companion social application sector, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected by SAMR as a registered address because market entity registration law requires actual fixed premises suitable for business operation, tax registration, legal service, and business books. Commercial banks in China will reject account opening if only a virtual office exists; municipal tax authorities similarly reject such an address for invoice management and administrative inspections. A physical office in the declared administrative district with a valid lease, utility bills, office signage, staff, and records is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: original lease, land-use certificate or building ownership certificate copy, utility bills, on-site signage, staffing roster, seating plan, IT equipment, business contracts, accounting records, and data-security policies. Unannounced physical inspection likelihood is high, estimated at 70-80% in the first year for internet and content-oriented WFOEs; municipal SAMR and tax authorities conduct targeted spot checks. Non-occupancy triggers abnormal operating address status, lifting of tax registration, and possible revocation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 7, 10, 16, 22, 24, 26-30, 32, 33, 40, 47-53, 57-60 and 178; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 4, 6, 28 and 29; Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration of the People's Republic of China (State Council Decree No. 746, effective 1 March 2022), Articles 6, 8, 13, 17, 18, 19 and 20
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), Company Registration Bureau, and the local Market Supervision Administration of the registered office in mainland China
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Company Establishment (SAMR uniform company establishment registration application form) together with the Articles of Association, shareholder identity credentials, registered office evidence, and statutory officer appointment documents
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a general wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company under the PRC Company Law 2023 and Foreign Investment Law 2020. The shareholders may fix the registered capital in the Articles of Association and must pay the subscribed capital in full by the agreed contribution deadline; cash contributions are subject to bank deposit verification. There is no mandatory escrow, blocked capital account, or capital call requirement at Stage 2 incorporation for this ISIC 6311 digital-services scope. If the company later enters a regulated value-added telecommunications or online audio-visual licensing regime, sector-specific minimum capital or license conditions may be separately imposed, but no such threshold is triggered by the current approved business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD

1. CONVENING AND QUORUM. The undersigned, being the entire Board of Directors of CN_WFOE_LTD (the Company), a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company proposed to be incorporated under the laws of the People's Republic of China, hereby waive all notice, formality, and physical meeting requirements pursuant to the Company Law and the future Articles of Association, and adopt the following resolutions by unanimous written consent. This resolution is effective immediately upon signature and shall constitute the complete governing mandate for the incorporation period.

2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The Board ratifies the registered capital of the Company, which is [insert amount in RMB or USD], divided into [insert number] ordinary shares, all of which are subscribed by the sole shareholder [insert shareholder name]. The Board approves the capital contribution schedule set out in the Articles of Association and directs the legal representative to open the necessary bank accounts and to cause the shareholder to fund its subscribed capital in cash or other lawful consideration no later than the contribution deadline specified in the Articles. The Board confirms that the shares have not been and shall not be offered to the public.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes and directs the legal representative to select a commercial bank approved by the People's Bank of China, to open a basic deposit account, a foreign currency settlement account, and any other required accounts, and to appoint authorized signatories, including the legal representative and the finance manager. All cheques, remittance instructions, loan documents, and deposit agreements shall require the signatures of any two authorized signatories or such combination as set out in a signing mandate approved by the Board.

4. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts the registered office located at [insert full registered address] as the Company's statutory address in China. The Board authorizes the legal representative to execute and deliver the lease, to procure the landlord's title or usage certificate, and to file the address with the State Administration for Market Regulation. The Board confirms that the registered office is suitable for maintaining statutory books and accounting records.

5. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints [insert name] as director and legal representative, [insert name] as director, [insert name] as supervisor, and [insert name] as general manager. Each appointee accepts the office and is authorized to perform all lawful acts required for company registration, tax registration, social insurance, and foreign exchange. The legal representative may delegate any administrative task; however, all contracts above [insert threshold] require joint signature. The Board directs all officers to proceed with the incorporation and to report the issuance of the business license to the next board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Registration and Entity Type Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service and local Municipal Market Supervision Administration one-window service center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Chinese company name and alternative names through the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Service or the local Market Supervision Administration one-window system. Select WFOE Limited Liability as the entity form and verify that the intended business scope is not on the Foreign Investment Negative List. The system will automatically screen identical, similar, or prohibited names. If the name is preliminarily approved, reserve it for six months and download the name pre-registration approval. All submissions must be made by a designated representative holding a valid power of attorney, with passport and identity verification completed through facial recognition or physical appearance at the service center.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese company name and up to three alternative names
Certificate of incorporation or business registration of the foreign shareholder
Passport or identity document of the ultimate beneficial owner if a natural person
Power of attorney appointing the local agent or designated representative
Foreign investor negative-list compliance statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, refile an alternative name within five working days through the same portal. If suspension is caused by similarity to an existing trademark or registered name, submit a trademark coexistence consent or adopt a distinctive invented name. If the foreign-investment restriction flag is raised, obtain a negative-list compliance opinion from a licensed Chinese lawyer before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutional Documents Preparation, Foreign Investor Legalization, and Registered Office Lease Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chinese embassy or consulate in the foreign investor's home country, the applicable Apostille authority under the Hague Apostille Convention, and the SAMR online pre-filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association, the capital contribution table, the shareholders' resolution, and the director appointment forms. The foreign shareholder's certificate of incorporation, resolutions, and identity credentials must be notarized in the home country and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate or apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention, with a reliable Chinese or English translation supplied where required. Verify the registered office address by obtaining a valid commercial lease and a copy of the owner's property ownership certificate or a landlord use letter. All original documents must be kept at the registered office, and the responsible person must ensure that the registered capital, contribution period, and liability clauses comply with the Company Law and the Foreign Investment Law. Submit a preliminary electronic copy for SAMR pre-check if the local system offers it.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder's certificate of incorporation with notarization or apostille and translation
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Shareholders' resolution on incorporation of the Company
Capital contribution schedule and bank remittance intention letter
Commercial lease contract and property ownership certificate or landlord consent
Power of attorney for the designated representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization or legalization is deemed inadequate, obtain re-notarization or a supplementary apostille from the home-country authority and resubmit. If SAMR queries the lease or capital contribution provisions, provide a supplemental declaration or amend the Articles of Association by a new shareholders' resolution and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (establishment registration division) via the SAMR online portal or the provincial enterprise one-stop service center, followed by the Public Security Bureau for seal recordal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the local SAMR online service or visit the municipal administrative service center. Complete the establishment registration application, upload all scanned and notarized documents, ensure that the legal representative signs the application form by real-name verification, and submit for SAMR review. The system will verify uniqueness of the name, legality of business scope, and sufficiency of capital commitments. No statutory filing fee is charged. Upon approval, the competent SAMR will issue a unified social credit code business license. The company must then apply within ten days to a licensed seal-carving company for the company seal, finance seal, invoice seal, contract seal, and legal representative seal, and record the seal specimens with the Public Security Bureau.
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration application form signed by the designated representative or legal representative
Articles of Association
Shareholders' resolution
Notarized or apostilled foreign investor documents
Lease contract and registered office evidence
Identity documents of legal representative and supervisor
Name pre-registration approval certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a deficiency notice, remedy the specified items within fifteen days. If the application is rejected due to name or business-scope issues, file a revised application with corrected wording. If a foreign investment negative list issue arises, restructure the entity or submit a compliance opinion from a licensed lawyer before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Social Insurance Registration, Foreign Exchange Capital Account, and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local tax service hall, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through a designated Chinese commercial bank, and the chosen commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days of receiving the business license, complete tax registration at the local tax authority, confirm the taxpayer type, handle invoice quota and e-invoice setup, and register corporate income tax and value-added tax. The legal representative must appear for biometric verification or use the electronic tax bureau. Open a corporate basic settlement account and a foreign exchange capital account with a designated bank; the foreign shareholder remits registered capital under the capital account, and the bank reports the foreign direct investment via SAFE's FDI registration system. Register the company's social insurance and housing provident fund if employees are hired, and file statutory labor contracts. Retain all capital remittance receipts and foreign direct investment registration forms as required.
required_dossiers: Business license original
Company seals and final seal specimen cards
Identity documents of legal representative and seal custodian
Articles of Association
Bank account opening application and authorization
Foreign shareholder remittance voucher
SAFE foreign direct investment registration confirmation
Tax registration form and taxpayer information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried for missing legal representative verification, reschedule biometric verification. If SAFE or FDI registration is delayed, submit the bank remittance voucher, capital receipt certificate, and Articles of Association to the designated bank for correction. If the remittance currency or reference code is incorrect, obtain a refund from the overseas bank and re-remit under the correct foreign exchange classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital service under ISIC 6311; no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, warehousing, or industrial installation exists in this entity scope, so no industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing agency has jurisdiction

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) environmental impact assessment clearance is not triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA required because there is no construction, industrial production, or physical emission source under the PRC Classification List of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the entity has no industrial wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emission stack, hazardous waste generation, or air pollutant discharge point. Only standard office electronic waste and municipal solid waste handling protocols apply in the ordinary office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable in the industrial licensing sense; a civil defense fire permit is not required for a pure software and voice-streaming services entity. The registered office, if used as an ordinary office, must still maintain basic fire prevention exits, portable fire extinguishers, and general workplace safety compliance under the local fire authority and work safety regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, exercised through provincial, municipal and district tax service bureaus; electronic compliance is conducted through the official e-Tax Bureau portal (https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn) and the STA Golden Tax Phase IV centralized digital tax-control system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE): (1) complete incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the integrated national enterprise registration platform and obtain the Business License carrying the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which becomes the WFOE's Chinese Tax Identification Number; (2) within 30 days of license issuance, complete tax registration with the competent local tax service bureau through the e-Tax Bureau portal or in-person counter, confirming registration with the provincial STA and filing the financial accounting system, bank account, legal representative and controlling foreign investor details; (3) determine VAT taxpayer status and, where annual taxable turnover reaches RMB 5,000,000 or where input VAT credit is desired, register as a VAT general taxpayer with the competent tax authority and obtain approval for official VAT fapiao issuance; (4) for a foreign non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment, the non-resident entity must separately apply for a Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Identification Number with the STA tax service bureau where the payor or property is located, or file through its authorized withholding agent, submitting the non-resident registration application, evidence of incorporation, contract evidencing China-source income, and withholding agent appointment documents; (5) complete foreign exchange registration with the relevant designated foreign exchange bank or through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) digital system for future export/import receipts and cross-border payment evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for income tax entity classification: the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law does not allow check-the-box pass-through elections, a Chinese-established WFOE is always a resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income, and no hybrid mismatch entity election is available. The only statutory elections relevant to indirect tax are the VAT small-scale taxpayer election for turnover below RMB 5,000,000 and the VAT general taxpayer election for entities wishing to credit input VAT, plus treaty-based reductions for non-resident shareholders where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the PRC VAT system, supplemented by the urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge and local education surcharge which are levied on VAT paid; voice streaming and social application services are characterized as modern/information technology services or value-added telecommunication services subject to the 6% VAT rate for domestic supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales is the statutory threshold for mandatory VAT general taxpayer registration; all enterprises engaged in taxable sales must complete basic tax registration upon establishment irrespective of turnover, and taxpayers below RMB 5,000,000 may voluntarily register as VAT general taxpayers. A WFOE with predominantly app-store digital services should register as a VAT general taxpayer to preserve input VAT credit eligibility and export/service zero-rating or exemption rights.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China does not operate a traditional per-transaction fiscal clearance device regime; however, the Golden Tax Phase IV system and the fully digitalized electronic invoice (digital e-invoice) reform require all VAT invoices to be issued through the official e-Tax Bureau digital invoice platform using STA-controlled invoice codes, 20-digit invoice numbers and a digitally stamped anti-fraud two-dimensional code. Transaction-level invoice data is transmitted to the STA in real time upon issuance. Large enterprises and certified electronic invoice service providers may use approved electronic invoice APIs, but all data ultimately clears through the STA e-Tax Bureau. Special VAT invoices for input crediting, export invoices and zero-rated/exempt service invoices must be issued within the statutory time limits and reported in the VAT filing return; no separate paper fiscal treasury stamp is used.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: physical exports from China customs territory qualify for the VAT zero rate and export tax rebate only when there is a formal outward customs declaration, actual departure of goods evidenced by a transport document, an export sale to a non-resident buyer, and receipt of foreign exchange proceeds by the WFOE; the WFOE must be a VAT general taxpayer with properly credited input VAT. Qualifying offshore digital services: the voice streaming and companion social application services may qualify for VAT zero-rating or exemption if they fall within the STA's cross-border taxable services rules, including under Notice Caishui [2016] No. 36 and the State Taxation Administration Announcement No. 53 of 2016 on cross-border taxable services exemption, provided the service is supplied to an overseas recipient, is completely consumed outside the PRC, does not relate to domestic persons, real estate or enterprises, and payment is received from outside China. For app-store distribution through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the WFOE must maintain platform store settlement reports, non-resident user download/geo-location evidence, and interface evidence showing the service is made available to offshore territories; services consumed by users located within the PRC are domestic supplies subject to VAT at the applicable rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (outward export customs declaration form with customs release endorsement, export license where applicable, and customs-assigned examination code)
Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal/air transport document proving physical export and offshore destination of the goods

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or, under current SAFE and bank digitalization practice, a designated foreign exchange bank receipt/export proceeds collection and settlement voucher evidencing the non-resident buyer's remittance and timely FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and customs/SAFE authorities jointly audit export VAT zero-rating and rebate claims. If a claim is unsupported by the required customs declaration, transport documents or foreign exchange receipt evidence, the tax authority will disallow the zero rate, claw back any refund already paid, and recharacterize the transaction as a domestic taxable supply. The taxpayer must then pay output VAT at the applicable rate plus late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the original due date. Under Article 66 of the Tax Collection Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, fraudulently obtaining export tax refunds by false export declarations or other deceptive means triggers recovery of the refund, a fine of 100% to 500% of the refund obtained, and suspension of the right to apply for export tax rebates for a prescribed period; where criminal liability is established, Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China imposes fines and imprisonment ranging up to life imprisonment for especially large fraud amounts. There is no limitation period for recovery of fraudulent export refunds, tax evasion or refusal to pay tax under Article 52 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, and retrospective clawback can therefore reach back beyond the ordinary five-year record retention period where fraud is proven.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime for the RMB with current account convertibility but strict capital account controls. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) engaged in voice streaming services must obtain all inbound foreign direct investment through a lawful FDI capital account, complete SAFE registration at the bank, and use a capital settlement account for RMB conversion purposes. Revenue derived from overseas app stores, including Apple App Store and Google Play, is treated as current account service income and can be received in a domestic foreign exchange current account, settled into RMB, or retained in FX, provided the transaction is genuine and backed by commercial agreements, invoices, and periodic settlement statements. Profit remittance to the foreign parent company is permitted once the WFOE has paid corporate income tax, prepared audited financial statements, obtained a tax payment certificate, and submitted a board resolution approving the dividend distribution. The bank will verify the authenticity, tax compliance, and beneficial ownership background before effecting the cross-border remittance. Capital account transactions, such as shareholder loans, equity transfers, or offshore guarantees, require additional SAFE approval and cannot be freely settled. Therefore, while service-related earnings are convertible on the current account, capital flows remain tightly controlled, and any attempt to route capital injection, intercompany loans, or profit repatriation without the required regulatory filings will be rejected by the relevant clearing bank and may trigger an SAFE penalty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE current account administration, export and cross-border service proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic foreign exchange account within the verification window established by the bank, generally within 90 days from the date of service completion or contractual billing for service exports, and within 90 days from the customs declaration for goods exports, unless an extension is approved by the bank under the trade financing supervision system. Mandatory conversion ratio is 0% - China no longer imposes compulsory surrender of foreign export proceeds to the central bank; however, 100% of export/service receipts must be received into a SAFE-supervised FX account and either retained or settled voluntarily through a designated licensed bank based on genuine underlying trade and service documents.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.repatriation_deadline_standard: 90 days from service completion or goods export declaration, subject to bank verification and possible extension for valid commercial reasons.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: General Foreign Exchange Current Account (Service Trade)
RMB Basic Deposit Account and Payment Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not legally authorized to hold client funds, open domestic settlement accounts, or perform foreign exchange conversion directly for a mainland China WFOE. Such EMIs lack a SAFE payment institution license and cannot act as a local clearing rail. They may technically collect app store proceeds overseas if they hold appropriate licenses in the merchant’s offshore intermediate jurisdiction, but the funds must ultimately be repatriated through a licensed Chinese commercial bank and reported to SAFE. Therefore, the WFOE must rely on a tier-1 domestic bank for all onshore clearing, capital verification, and FX settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory. Statutory legal representatives and ultimate beneficial owners, if non-resident, must either appear in person at a bank branch in mainland China for a face-to-face KYC interview, or provide a notarized and consular-legalized Power of Attorney authorizing a Chinese resident representative to attend the interview on their behalf. Some tier-1 banks permit a remote video interview for foreign directors, provided the company has an established physical lease in China, the director’s passport is notarized abroad, and all corporate documents are apostilled or legalized through the Chinese embassy or consulate. However, due to FATF standards and SAFE enforcement, the bank’s compliance committee usually requires the WFOE’s statutory legal representative or board-appointed senior manager to be physically present for the high-risk opening procedure. The exception is when the shareholder is itself a regulated financial institution or listed entity with full external audit trail, in which case remote opening may be approved under strict documentary conditions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of the offshore parent is located in a tax haven or discretionary trust structure with no clear economic profile, creating an unacceptable source-of-wealth opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address for each natural person UBO; trust deed or declaration of trust; certificate of incumbency from the registered agent; group organizational chart showing all intermediate holding companies; audited financial statements of the immediate parent and ultimately controlled entity; bank reference letters from the primary offshore bank; and a legal opinion from a reputable law firm establishing the commercial rationale and ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection originates from an unrelated third-party payment remitter or a jurisdiction with high money-laundering risk, triggering suspicion of third-party funding or layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized share subscription agreement; board resolutions approving capital contribution; source-of-funds bank statements for the preceding 12 months; proof that the remitting account belongs to the direct shareholder; SAFE foreign direct investment (FDI) registration certificate; capital verification report issued by a Chinese certified public accountant; and a signed memorandum explaining the intra-group funding chain with supporting loan or equity agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: App store revenue flows from Apple and Google using intermediary marketplaces or commission structures that do not match contractual royalties, creating transaction-pattern mismatch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; monthly payout and settlement statements from Apple and Google; bank statements showing the credited amounts; the WFOE’s service fee schedule or IP royalty model; invoices issued by the WFOE to offshore customers; corporate income tax returns and VAT filings demonstrating declared revenue; and a detailed reconciliation memo mapping net payouts to agreed commercial terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE appears to be a shell company with no physical office, no local employees, and no operational substance in China.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease agreement in mainland China with rent payment evidence; utility bills and site photographs; social insurance contribution records and payroll payroll bank statements for employees; information technology infrastructure asset listings; registered ICP filing or relevant telecom/business licenses; minutes of board meetings held in China; and a corporate operational narrative showing the KYC-required business continuity plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the direct offshore shareholder’s bank account to the WFOE’s FDI Capital Account at a SAFE-designated tier-1 bank. The payment instruction must clearly reference the purpose code for foreign direct investment, the shareholder name, the WFOE name, and the SAFE FDI registration number. Upon receipt, the bank will conduct authenticity screening; the funds are then placed in the capital settlement account for conversion into RMB at prevailing rates. A Chinese certified public accountant performs capital verification and issues a capital verification report, which is filed with SAFE and the market regulation authority. No capital injection may be converted to RMB until the capital verification and SAFE filing are completed. For all app store revenue and service trade receipts, the international parent or intermediate entity must remit via SWIFT with the appropriate service trade purpose code and the underlying commercial invoice, so that the bank can apply the current account clearing procedure and avoid unnecessary holds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements must be made through a licensed domestic bank using SWIFT MT103 for corporate service payments, dividends, IP royalties, and intercompany operating expenses; Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) and Documentary Collections are reserved for physical goods procurement and vendor financing where trade documents such as commercial invoices, bills of lading, and inspection certificates are required. For each outbound transaction, the bank will require the underlying contract, commercial invoice, tax withholding certificate, board resolution where applicable, and SAFE reporting through the bank’s foreign exchange monitoring system. Payments for profit distribution are cleared only after tax settlement and issuance of the tax payment certificate by the State Taxation Administration. All outbound wires must reflect the true commercial purpose; otherwise the bank will reject or suspend the payment and escalate the matter to SAFE.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD forward contracts with genuine current account or trade exposure, approved by SAFE and executed with a domestic licensed bank
Onshore FX swaps for liquidity and working capital management associated with real cross-border transaction flows
Currency swaps for longer-term corporate debt or FDI-related exposures, subject to SAFE registration and approval
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore within China; only offshore NDFs may be used by non-resident counterparties, and the WFOE cannot enter such contracts without SAFE approval
Plain-vanilla FX options with physical delivery are permissible where the WFOE can prove genuine transaction exposure and obtains bank-level compliance approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Publicity Report (annual report to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year from January 1 to June 30, covering data for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by June 30 places the WFOE in the List of Enterprises Operating under Abnormal Status; administrative fine of RMB 5,000-30,000 (approx. USD 700-4,200) may be imposed; continued non-compliance for three consecutive years results in inclusion in the Serious Violation of Law and Breach of Trust List and potential revocation/administrative strike-off of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (annual foreign investment information report under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting rules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and local commerce authorities, submitted through the integrated SAMR annual-reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year from January 1 to June 30 for the preceding fiscal year; changes to foreign ownership during the year must be reported within 20 working days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or false submission triggers an order by MOFCOM to rectify within a fixed period; non-compliance after rectification order can result in fines up to RMB 100,000 (approx. USD 14,000) for enterprises, publication of violation information, and linkage to the SAMR abnormal-status/revocation mechanism for chronic non-reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Annual Filing (Enterprise Income Tax annual declaration and final settlement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) at the local in-charge tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the following calendar year after the end of each tax year (December 31); monthly or quarterly instalments are payable within 15 days after each period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is punishable by a fine of up to RMB 2,000, or up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases; unpaid tax bears daily late-payment interest of 0.05%; continued default may lead to tax authority enforcement (asset seizure, restricted exit/clearance) and, together with recurrent violations, administrative license revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Certified Public Accountant Audit Report and Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' annual general meeting; a signed paper copy must be retained at the registered office and be immediately available to SAMR and tax authority inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by April 30 (professional corporate-secretarial deadline for shareholder review), and in all cases no later than June 30 to support the SAMR annual-report filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to procure the statutory audit breaches the PRC Company Law; regulators may order rectification; absence of an audit report invalidates the SAMR annual-report filing and exposes the WFOE to abnormal listing, fines for directors/officers and, for repeated annual-report violations, strike-off/revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Every PRC-registered limited-liability WFOE is subject to mandatory annual CPA audit with no size-based exemption. PRC Company Law requires all companies to prepare annual financial reports and have them audited by an independent certified public accounting firm at the end of each fiscal year. There are no statutory balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount de-minimis thresholds: a shell WFOE with total assets of RMB 0, revenue of RMB 0 and 0 employees is still audited. SAMR's risk-based annual-report inspections commonly prioritise enterprises with annual operating revenue of at least RMB 10 million, total assets of at least RMB 20 million or more than 50 employees, but these inspection-selection triggers are not the legal audit trigger; the legal audit trigger is the simple fact of incorporation/running a WFOE in China.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/China GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS; eligible small enterprises may apply the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards (SEAS). WFOEs must keep statutory books in RMB and Chinese. The WFOE's group consolidation may use IFRS at parent level, but the PRC statutory-reporting package is ASBE-based and may not be replaced by IFRS-only filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not maintain a standalone UBO register. The annual confirmation of beneficial ownership is embedded in the SAMR annual enterprise report and the MOFCOM annual foreign investment information report, both due between January 1 and June 30 each year; these filings capture actual controllers and ultimate beneficial shareholders. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership triggers a 30-day registration window at SAMR (from the date of the equity transfer/board resolution) and a 20-working-day change-report window under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting rules; failure to record the transfer makes the transfer ineffective against third parties and triggers the delinquency penalties described in the annual compliance matrix.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,500 per year for a Tier-1 city registered-office compliance service; USD 300 - USD 800 per year in Tier-2/Tier-3 cities.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 6,000 for a small/mid WFOE; USD 10,000 - USD 25,000 where group audit, transfer-pricing documentation, or consolidated reporting is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential rates and incentives include: 15% reduced rate for High and New Technology Enterprises certified under State Council standards; 5% effective rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million; 15% encouraged-industry rate in Hainan Free Trade Port and certain western regions; 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; accelerated depreciation for specific fixed assets; and statutory exemption or reduced rate treatments for qualified software enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Class A) and associated schedules, including A105000 Tax Adjustment Schedule, A105080 Depreciation and Amortization Schedule, A107012 R&D Additional Deduction Schedule, A108000 Foreign Tax Credit Schedule, and related-party transaction disclosure schedules, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration eTax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual CIT settlement return with quarterly provisional prepayments during the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT payment due within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end; annual CIT filing and final settlement due within 5 months of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by May 31 for a calendar-year enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from voice streaming, virtual gifts, paid subscriptions, advertising, digital content licensing, and ancillary services, stated before VAT but after deduction of real trade discounts and sales returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile gross billings with Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement statements; do not net app-store commissions against revenue unless the WFOE is contractually an agent. If revenue is earned through an overseas affiliate, support the intercompany margin with a transfer pricing benchmark and disclose the related-party transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to revenue, including content licensing fees, streamer compensation, bandwidth, data hosting, in-app content acquisition, and customer service costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border content licensing fees and service fees paid to foreign affiliates must be supported by written agreements, actual service evidence, arm's-length pricing, and withholding tax vouchers; amounts lacking economic substance are non-deductible for CIT purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chinese local taxes and surcharges, such as urban construction and maintenance tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp duty, real estate tax, and land use tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT is not deductible in the CIT computation; VAT withheld and paid on behalf of non-resident suppliers must not duplicate-deduct, and contractual gross-up clauses must be treated consistently with the withholding agent's statutory obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: User acquisition, advertising, influencer and streamer incentives, promotion fees, app store commissions, traffic-purchase costs, and platform rebate expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offshore marketing and traffic-agency fees create permanent establishment exposure if the foreign service provider habitually concludes contracts in China or maintains a fixed place; treaty business-profits protection must be documented and withholding tax considered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General corporate overheads, executive and staff salaries, social insurance, rent, office expenses, legal and professional fees, and IT administration costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees paid to non-resident directors, consultants, and management companies are subject to China-source income withholding where the services are performed in China; related-party management fees must pass arm's-length and substance tests and cannot merely reallocate headquarters costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense on bank loans, related-party loans, and other financing costs, net of interest income, foreign exchange gains or losses, and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to foreign lenders is subject to statutory WHT on interest at 10% unless treaty-reduced; the thin-capitalisation rule restricts deductible related-party debt to a 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio; interest exceeding the safe harbour is non-deductible unless additional evidentiary requirements are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recognition of impairment losses on receivables, inventories, fixed assets, goodwill, and other assets based on accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CIT permits deduction only when impairment is demonstrated with objective evidence and, for related-party receivables, a bona fide collection process; tax authorities may challenge write-offs of receivables due from non-resident shareholders as disguised profit distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net gains or losses on financial assets measured at fair value through profit or loss, including derivative positions and convertible instruments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Derivative and hedging transactions with overseas affiliates must be priced on arm's-length terms and disclosed in the transfer pricing documentation; crypto-asset gains or losses are not generally usable because of PRC cryptocurrency restrictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend income, interest income from investments, profit distributions from associates and joint ventures, and disposal gains or losses on equity investments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from a Chinese resident enterprise by the WFOE are tax-exempt if the subsidiary is also a resident enterprise; dividends from a non-resident affiliate are taxable with foreign tax credit relief, and no exemption applies merely because the WFOE is a pass-through for foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting operating profit derived as revenue less cost, taxes, selling, administrative and financial expenses, adjusted for impairment, fair value movements, and investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the operating profit is not artificially reduced by charges from the foreign parent. If the WFOE earns only routine distribution or service remuneration, the profit margin must align with the documented functional analysis and the relevant TNMM or profit-split position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gains on disposal of non-current assets, government subsidies, compensation income, penalty receipts, and other items outside ordinary business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Government subsidies received from PRC authorities are generally taxable unless specifically excluded; cross-border recharges of such subsidies to non-resident affiliates are not permitted unless a genuine taxable service was provided and CIGA substance supports the allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net losses on disposal of non-current assets, charitable donations within deductible limits, flood relief contributions, penalties, fines, and other non-business outlays.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Statutory fines, tax penalties, illegal payments, and penalties payable to foreign regulators are non-deductible; donations to non-resident organisations are generally not deductible unless made through Approved PRC charitable channels.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting total profit before corporate income tax, computed as operating profit plus non-operating income less non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This accounting figure is the starting point for CIT reconciliation; any book-tax differences arising from foreign exchange gains on intercompany loans or from conversion of non-resident owner equity in shares must be supported by corroborating accounting policies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying tax adjustment additions, tax adjustment deductions, tax-exempt income, additional deductions, previous-year loss carryforward, and required special tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE cannot offset foreign-related expenses where the corresponding income is exempt; the adjustment process must include Schedule A105000 entries for transfer-pricing adjustments, unreasonably allocated head-office expenses, and disallowed non-resident withholding penalties. Loss carryforward is limited to 5 years except for specified high-tech and pioneer industries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT rate applied to taxable income, normally 25%, 15% for qualified High and New Technology Enterprises, or the small low-profit effective rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise; the applicable rate does not depend on the foreign parent's residence. Incorrectly applying a foreign preferential rate on China-source income is a common fatal error. Any reduced rate must be evidenced by an effective HNTE certificate or pre-filing confirmation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed as taxable income multiplied by the applicable CIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax payable must include China-source income earned through the WFOE; no credit is available at this line for taxes paid by the foreign parent, and no deduction is allowed for the 10% withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign income taxes paid on foreign-source income included in the Chinese taxable income, capped at the Chinese CIT payable on such foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE may claim direct and indirect foreign tax credits for PRC tax on dividends repatriated from foreign subsidiaries; supporting forms and jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction baskets are required. Foreign taxes on income that is not reported in China cannot be credited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net CIT payable after foreign tax credits and other deductible tax credits, but before deducting provisional payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the amount on which WFOE must settle with the State Taxation Administration; if the WFOE has not paid sufficient provisional tax, interest and late-payment surcharges apply from the statutory due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Instalments of CIT prepaid for Q1 through Q4 of the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepayments must be based on actual accounting profit or a tax-authority-approved base; underpaying provisional tax while claiming foreign treaty benefits may result in interest and administrative sanctions. The WFOE should reconcile prepayments with the annual return's current-period profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 20 - Net Tax Payable or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between actual annual CIT payable and total provisional prepayments, giving the final balance due to the State Taxation Administration or refund receivable to the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a refund arises from overpaid quarterly CIT, do not repatriate the refund to the foreign parent before CIT has been judicial reviewed; distribution of refunds to non-resident shareholders remains subject to dividend WHT where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without reasonable cause: RMB 2,000 fine, increased up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases, plus forced filing order. Underpaid tax: daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue amount. Fraudulent or misleading filing: recovery of underpaid tax, penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded amount, and criminal referral in the presence of intentional tax evasion or false VAT invoices. Tax authorities may also publicize serious violations and blacklist the enterprise, resulting in coordinated credit restrictions and travel bans on legal representatives and responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory reduced rate (Enterprise Income Tax Law nominal 20% reduced by Implementing Regulation to 10%) for dividends distributed by the WFOE to its non-resident shareholder, unless an applicable bilateral tax treaty or arrangement reduces the rate, commonly to 5% for a beneficial corporate shareholder holding at least 25% of the WFOE's capital, or to 0% under limited special non-resident dividend exemption protocols only where separately approved.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The WFOE, as the distribution entity, acts as statutory withholding agent. To apply treaty relief, before effecting remittance the non-resident shareholder or withholding agent must file an application through the State Taxation Administration electronic portal under SAT Announcement No. 35 (2019), submit an original or certified Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty counterparty tax authority for the period concerned, provide a complete Beneficial Ownership self-assessment using the factors in SAT Announcement No. 9 (2018), and evidence that the shareholder is not a shell or conduit: corporate registry documents, financial statements, number of employees, office leases, business board resolutions, and proof of substantive economic activities. The beneficial owner must generally hold the required minimum shareholding continuously for at least 12 months for reduced dividend rates, and the Chinese tax authority may request supplementary documentation before accepting the reduced rate. If relief is denied, the WFOE must make good the shortfall of 10% WHT plus statutory interest and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest from China to non-resident enterprises are subject to statutory EIT withholding at 10%, plus VAT where applicable on imported services and royalties (generally 6% VAT for royalties and certain financial services, unless exemption applies). DTA rates commonly reduce EIT withholding: for example, the China-Hong Kong arrangement and China-Singapore treaty generally grant 5% dividends to qualifying corporate owners, 7% interest, and 5% royalties to beneficial owners. Claims for treaty-reduced royalty or interest rates require the same TRC and beneficial-ownership proof as dividend relief, and must not exceed the amount that would be paid to a third party.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The WFOE must prepare Local File documentation if its annual related-party transactions reach any of these thresholds: RMB 200 million for tangible-asset transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible-asset transfers, RMB 100 million for financial-asset transfers, or RMB 40 million for related-party services (SAT Announcement No. 42 [2016]). Master File documentation is additionally mandated when cross-border related-party revenue or aggregate related-party transactions exceed the statutory RMB 1 billion threshold or when the enterprise is selected by the tax authority.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not apply a standalone zero-tax Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but it enforces economic substance through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under EIT Law Article 47, the 2018 Beneficial Ownership Rules, and treaty abuse doctrines. For a WFOE, the tax authorities will test whether the entity performs entrepreneurial functions, owns or controls unique intangibles, manages commercial risks, and conducts its Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) by having management, employees, physical assets, and board decisions in China. A shell WFOE that merely signs paper contracts while the foreign parent makes all strategic and operational decisions risks being denied treaty benefits, having intercompany royalties disregarded, and facing permanent establishment scenarios in the architecturally high-tax jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Unreported Cross-Border Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE underreports in-app sales of virtual gifts and paid subscriptions from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, uses fabricated influencer invoices to inflate deductible costs, pays offshore management fees to a zero-tax affiliate without any actual service, and intentionally keeps profits in overseas nominees to avoid recognition of China-source revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the PRC Tax Collection Law Article 32, late tax bears a daily surcharge of 0.05%; Article 63 imposes recovery of unpaid tax and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the amount evaded. Criminal Law Article 201 criminalizes tax evasion: imprisonment up to 3 years with a fine where the evaded amount is relatively large and exceeds 10% of the tax payable, or imprisonment of 3 to 7 years where the amount is enormous and exceeds 30%. Criminal Law Article 205 adds criminal liability for falsely issued VAT invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil where directors or shareholders commingle assets, create a mere façade, or grossly abuse the limited-liability structure to evade taxes. The responsible legal representative and directors face personal civil asset restitution, freezing of personal bank accounts, travel bans and blacklisting by the tax authority, and potential criminal imprisonment under Criminal Law Articles 201 and 205. If the corporate form has been abused to shirk tax obligations, shareholders may be held jointly and severally liable for all unpaid CIT, WHT, penalties, and surcharges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse and Artificial Shell-Holding Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is held through an intermediary company in Hong Kong or another treaty jurisdiction that has no office, no employees, no commercial risk and no independent decision-making, solely to obtain the lower 5% dividend WHT or 5% royalty WHT instead of the statutory 10% China-source withholding rate; the arrangement is artificial and lacks reasonable commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 47 and its implementing rules grant the tax authority the power to recharacterize or disregard transactions lacking reasonable commercial purpose; Article 48 imposes interest on the underpaid tax. SAT Announcement No. 9 (2018) denies treaty benefits where the beneficial owner is not substantive. The applicable sanction is an upward CIT adjustment, restoration of the 10% WHT, late-payment surcharges at 0.05% per day, and, where false documents were submitted, a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Tax Collection Law Article 64.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who personally designed the sham holding chain may be personally liable for the WFOE's under-withheld tax when the entity is treated as their alter ego. Remedies include civil asset tracing and restitution, seizure of personal assets for corporate tax debts, restrictions on exit, denial of visa status or tax-residence certification, and criminal liability if the treaty abuse was a deliberate scheme to evade tax. A director found guilty of tax evasion through the shell arrangement may receive imprisonment under Criminal Law Article 201.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Payment-Channel Abuse in In-App Voice Commerce
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The voice-streaming app fails to carry out customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership screening, permits users to purchase virtual currency or gifts through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing as a disguised transfer of value, allows off-platform settlement of tips to third-party bank accounts without source-of-funds verification, and deliberately monitors only gross in-app metrics so that structured tipping patterns from sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions remain undetected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law imposes rectification orders, confiscation of illegal gains, and financial penalties on institutions, with aggravating sanctions including fines up to RMB 5 million for severe violations and licence revocations; directly responsible directors and AML compliance officers face personal fines. Criminal Law Article 191 (money laundering) punishes conduct that conceals or disguises the criminal origin of proceeds with imprisonment for up to 10 years and criminal fines. Ancillary liability also arises under the Cybersecurity Law and Data Security Law for unlawful processing of user-financial data without consent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly permit the app to be used as a money-laundering conduit cannot hide behind the corporate limited-liability shield. Courts may pierce the veil and order restitution of laundered assets from personal holdings; authorities may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and exit controls. Individuals who facilitate laundering, use shell treasury accounts, or approve anonymous settlement transfers face personal criminal imprisonment under Criminal Law Article 191, disqualification from acting as directors, and civil joint liability for damages suffered by the company or defrauded users.
